slides.title: Key questions

paragraphs.text: Key questions
Should Palisade raise prices at renewal in 2027 while churn is rising, and if so on which segments and by how much, to grow ARR at least 15% and keep net revenue retention above 100%?
Is rising churn a sign that customers reject our prices?
Which segments can take a price rise in 2027?
How much ARR does each option add, and does it meet the 2027 objectives?
How should the rise be sequenced, tested and monitored?
Decision maker
Success criteria
Timing
Out of scope
CEO Ravi Menon with the leadership team, approving the 2027 pricing plan
ARR grows at least 15% in 2027, from $86.0M to about $98.9M; Net revenue retention stays above 100% overall; The price change does not push churn up outside the promotion cohort
Leadership meeting, December 2026
Repackaging and new tiers; New-customer acquisition plan; Enterprise contracts renewing after 2027

slides.title: Executive summary

paragraphs.text: Executive summary
Raise mid-market and enterprise prices in 2027, and hold SMB until the promotion cohort is fixed and a price test passes
Churn is rising mainly in the 2025 SMB promotion cohort, not in the core customer base
–	Promotion customers explain about 91% of the rise in SMB churn
–	Onboarding is unlikely to cut SMB churn by much more than a third
Mid-market can likely take 10% and enterprise 7%, but SMB faces Inkwell's cheaper plan
–	A 10% higher mid-market price converted at 23.1%, against 23.6% (2024 test)
–	Our SMB win rate against Inkwell fell from 51% to 38% in a year
A targeted rise adds about $4.2M; 12% on every plan adds about $6.7M, not $10.3M, at more risk
–	Only 76% of ARR renews in 2027, so the CFO's $10.3M cannot all arrive
–	If retention holds, new customers need to add only about $0.8M to hit 15%
Decide in December, raise mid-market and enterprise from January, and test SMB first
–	Keep the 2,100 promotion customers out of the rise
–	Stop the SMB rollout if extra churn nears twice the 2023 response
